headline: Test with 2 million decoy secrets finds leaks in AI routers
pages: Researcher HD Moore sent nearly two million AI prompts containing unique decoy secrets through services that broker requests between apps and AI models, then watched where the secrets ended up. These AI routers, such as OpenRouter and Vercel, pick a model based on price or suitability. The decoys included unused Amazon Web Services keys, passwords, and unique web addresses and repository references, each placed in a single prompt sent to one provider so any leak could be traced. Ars Technica reports the results were poor. At least three AI providers appeared to have been compromised by attackers who siphoned prompts.

Several resellers logged prompts and passed them to people who then used the credentials. Some providers also ignored privacy settings such as Zero Data Retention and no data collection. Why it matters: developers who route prompts through intermediaries may be exposing sensitive data without knowing it. Source: Ars Technica.
